requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

The README documents this, so it is recorded and acceptable.

findings.claim: The core acceptance criterion is not met: a formatted type `T` declared in a referenced assembly gets no formatter. The collector rejects any data type whose `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty. That is true for every type loaded from a metadata reference, which is the normal case when Project B references Project A's DLL. In that case MsgPack021 ('data type not supported') is reported and nothing is generated. The user's partial class is then left without `Serialize`/`Deserialize` and the build fails. The feature only works when `T` is declared in source in the same compilation, which is the opposite of the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterForReferencedAssemblyTypeTests.FormatterIsGeneratedForTypeFromMetadataReference. ProjectA is emitted to a PE image and referenced from ProjectB via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. Expect MsgPack021 among the generator diagnostics, plus CS0535 in the output compilation, so the test fails on head.

findings.claim: The criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not implemented. Without a surrogate, `CreateContractlessMembers` always serializes every public read-write member by name as a string key and never reads attributes on `T`. Ignored attributes include `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`, `[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]`. A `T` with `[MessagePackObject]` + `[Key(0)]` therefore gets map-mode string keys instead of int keys, and members marked `[IgnoreMember]`, or left out of a `[DataContract]`, are serialized anyway. The SurrogateType path replaces this criterion rather than meeting it; ledger L18 says 'follow the requirement'.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests: both methods assert that no generated source mentions the excluded member 'Secret'. On head the contractless member list includes Secret, so both fail. (generated tests: DataContractMembershipIsHonoured, MessagePackIgnoreMemberIsHonoured)

findings.claim: The core requirement fails. `Collect` rejects any data type whose `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, and that is true for every type that comes from a referenced assembly (a metadata symbol). So for `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>`, where `ProjectA.MyType` lives in a referenced DLL, the generator reports MsgPack021 and emits no body. The partial class then fails to compile with CS0535. Only types declared in the same compilation work, which is exactly the case the feature was not needed for.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterReferencedAssemblyTests.FormatterIsGeneratedForTypeFromReferencedAssembly. It compiles ProjectA to an image, references it from ProjectB and drives the generator. On head it gets MsgPack021 plus CS0535 errors.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored when no SurrogateType is given. `CreateContractlessMembers` takes every public read-write member regardless of `[IgnoreMember]`, `[Key]` or `[MessagePackObject]`, and always uses string keys. Example: a T with `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(0)] Id` and `[IgnoreMember] IgnoredSecret` gets a map-mode formatter that serializes IgnoredSecret. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured', and the wire format differs from T's own formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterReferencedAssemblyTests.FormatterHonoursIgnoreMemberOnFormattedType. On head the generated MyTypeFormatter source contains 'IgnoredSecret'.

hunches.claim: The contractless mode only emits public read-write members, so public get-only properties and readonly fields are skipped. ContractlessStandardResolver (the dynamic mode users have today) includes these members, which are serialized and restored through a constructor. A user switching to this attribute would get different wire content. Separately, a class with no parameterless constructor is rejected with MsgPack005 and gets no formatter at all.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with `public int A {get;set;}` and `public int B {get;}` (set in the constructor) using ContractlessStandardResolver, then using the generated formatter. Compare the bytes; the generated output will lack key B.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode sorts members by ordinal name, and it ignores any [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes on T. The requirement says T's own attributes must be honoured when present. The implementation honours only surrogate attributes, so a T with [Key] or [DataMember] gets contractless string keys. This differs from the dynamic resolver's output for the same T.

receipt_plan.detail: Take a T annotated with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] in a referenced assembly. Serialize it with the dynamic resolver, then with the [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter. The dynamic output is an array, while the generated output is a map with name keys.

hunches.claim: The attribute-based exclusion of user-declared formatters in the hand-written formatter scan runs per candidate class. Hand-written formatters that happen to be partial and annotated are now silently dropped from the generated resolver. Also, the diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are Error severity and are newly reported only for opted-in classes, so this should not affect existing users. However, Collect is called without an accessibility guard on the generated partial's own declared accessibility: the template emits `partial class` with no accessibility modifier. Combined with the user's `public partial class`, the generated formatter may be inaccessible if the formatter is nested, or its resolver registration may not compile in an internal resolver.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test with a public partial formatter annotated with the attribute, plus a resolver-generating assembly. Check that the generated resolver references the formatter correctly and that the build has no errors.

hunches.claim: Generated code for a user-declared formatter is emitted without regard to MessagePackSecurity. Serialization is generated but the contractless string-key path relies on the same generated deserializer that applies options.Security.DepthStep. This was not verified here and the diff does not show that the depth step is skipped, so no concrete issue is established. One checkable concern: a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class with a surrogate silently drops members (via IgnoreMember or unkeyed ones), which is not a security hole.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator snapshot tests for a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class and confirm the generated Deserialize calls options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader) and DepthStep decrement in finally, matching the standard string-key/int-key templates.

hunches.claim: Collector rejects types with no declaring syntax (metadata-only) in GeneratedFormatterCollector, yet the requirement's whole point is T in a referenced assembly. `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` is true for any type from a referenced assembly (incl. ExternalPerson), so MsgPack021 would be reported and no formatter generated; this contradicts the requirement. Note L11 says metadata types are deliberately not formatted by default analysis, but the explicit attribute is the opt-in the requirement asks for, so L11 does not excuse this.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests (ExecutionTests references ExternalTypes assembly): ExternalPerson formatter should fail to generate / MsgPack021 reported because DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty for metadata types.

hunches.claim: Requirement says if T carries MessagePack attributes (e.g. [DataContract], [MessagePackObject], [Key]) they are honoured; the collector ignores attributes on T entirely and always uses contractless or surrogate. Acceptance criterion unmet.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator test where T has [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)] int keys on a property and a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class; assert the generated formatter uses int keys, which will fail since contractless string keys are used.

hunches.claim: The new GeneratedMessagePackFormatter attribute is documented and diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added to release notes and docs, so conventions are followed; however no generator snapshot tests cover successful generation output for the new formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun generator snapshot tests; no snapshot exists for a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] success case.

hunches.claim: The formatter's own MessagePack attributes are never honoured, but the requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they must be used. No test puts [MessagePackObject]/[Key] on T and checks the output. The collector ignores T's attributes and uses contractless or surrogate mode only.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] members, put a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class over it, and assert integer-key array output. Expected to fail because the output is a string-key map.

hunches.claim: The contractless test types have no case with public fields, private members, or inherited members. The ordering, IsPublicReadWrite and GetInstanceMembers logic are only exercised through two public get/set properties. Only the get-only Doubled case is covered.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:219 negate-condition: field.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public -> != Accessibility.Public; expected to survive because no test type has a public or private field.

hunches.claim: The surrogate execution test only asserts array length 8 and the Id, Name and Internal round-trip. It never checks that Id is at index 3 and Name at index 7, so a mutation that remaps keys, such as using the member index instead of intKey, would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:177 swap-boolean/delete-statement: CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey, ...) -> intKey: members.Count; the max-key 8 count differs, but a swap of the two keys would survive. Expected to survive because slot positions are never asserted.

hunches.claim: Diagnostics MsgPack021 for inaccessible, generic or struct types, MsgPack005 for a missing parameterless constructor, duplicate surrogate keys (KeysMustBeUnique) and MemberNeedsKey for an unkeyed surrogate member have no tests. Only the abstract case is tested, so mutating the other guards would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:75 remove-guard: delete the !compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter) clause; expected to survive because only the abstract-type case is tested.

hunches.claim: The test that GeneratedFormatterRegistered only checks that the exclusion from the hand-written formatter list works indirectly via IsType. No test covers the GeneratorUtilities attribute filter on its own. A mutant that removes the filter might still pass because the resolver would register the formatter anyway, or it might cause a duplicate that is not asserted.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: delete the !symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...) clause; check whether the execution tests still pass.

hunches.claim: The generator snapshot tests never exercise the success path, so the template change that emits `partial class` and the IsUserDeclaredFormatter flag are covered only by the execution tests. The diagnostic tests hand-write the members, and there is no generator output snapshot for the user-declared formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests snapshot suite and check that no snapshot contains a generated partial formatter; the string-key template path is also unverified for an unsealed partial class.

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter class itself. If the formatter is nested in a non-partial containing type, the template's EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces wraps the generated `partial class` in a re-declaration of the outer type. That likely yields CS0260 (missing partial on the outer type) rather than a clean MsgPack019 diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Read IsPartial (only symbol.DeclaringSyntaxReferences of the formatter is checked) together with the FormatterTemplate using EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces. To confirm, declare `class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> { } }` and check for CS0260.

hunches.claim: The new diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added to the analyzer's SupportedDiagnostics, but nothing in the diff updates AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md or adds doc/analyzers pages. The help links point to missing docs. The RS2000 release-tracking analyzer would fail the build with warnings-as-errors.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md has no MsgPack019-022 entries; the build would report RS2000.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Implements contractless-by-default plus an optional SurrogateType property on the attribute (surrogate keys by name), ignoring MessagePack attributes on T.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Contractless-only core: no SurrogateType; honour [DataContract]/[MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes already on T when present, falling back to contractless when absent.
